intro: Everything behind the assistant, from where the data comes from to the ways people reach it. Click a box to trace what it is built from. Tools this deployment does not offer, and sources it has not connected, are left out; the counts are those of the library being served.

nodes.name: Publication list
nodes.detail: The cluster's own list of its publications, the DOIs every other part of the library hangs on.

nodes.name: Metadata registries
nodes.detail: Abstracts, authors, journals and citation counts for the listed DOIs.

nodes.name: Full-text PDFs
nodes.detail: Open-access copies fetched per DOI, plus PDFs supplied through institutional access for what is paywalled.

nodes.name: PI pages
nodes.detail: The principal investigators' pages: group, institution, research focus and their publications.

nodes.name: Funding proposal
nodes.detail: The cluster's own proposal, converted to Markdown with a separate summary.

nodes.name: Crossref and OpenAlex
nodes.detail: Metadata for a DOI the library does not hold, to place it among the cluster's papers. Answers and failures are cached, and a service that throttles is left alone as long as it asked.

nodes.name: NOMAD API
nodes.detail: The public NOMAD materials-data repository, searched at call time; nothing is cached.

nodes.name: Bundle builder
nodes.detail: Collects the sources into the library files: merges the DOI list with the registries, extracts the full texts, profiles the PIs, builds the co-authorship graph and embeds every abstract. The bundle's file layout is the contract between it and the package.

nodes.name: cra library build
nodes.detail: Projects the paper vectors to two dimensions and clusters them for the publication map. Everything expensive happens here, never while serving.

nodes.name: cra library manifest
nodes.detail: Records a checksum per file and the expected counts. cra serve refuses a bundle that does not match its manifest.

nodes.name: cra library activate
nodes.detail: With a versioned root, a new bundle (uploaded in the console or installed by hand) is unpacked beside the live one, verified in full, and swapped in by moving one link. Rolling back is moving it again.

nodes.name: papers.csv
nodes.detail: One row per publication: DOI, title, authors, year, journal and dataset links. The only file a bundle must have.

nodes.name: abstracts.json
nodes.detail: Abstracts and registry metadata keyed by DOI, merged into each paper.

nodes.name: fulltexts.json
nodes.detail: Full-text bodies keyed by DOI, with where each came from. Reachable only in the chat, never through the outward MCP endpoint.

nodes.name: pis.json
nodes.detail: Principal investigators: group, institution, research focus and the DOIs of their publications.

nodes.name: embeddings.npz
nodes.detail: One vector per paper and the model that made them. A query is encoded with the same model or semantic search stays off.

nodes.name: graph.json
nodes.detail: The co-authorship graph between PIs, weighted by shared papers.

nodes.name: proposal.md
nodes.detail: The whole proposal as Markdown. Reachable only in the chat.

nodes.name: proposal_summary.md
nodes.detail: The proposal's summary, given to the model with every chat.

nodes.name: publication_map.json
nodes.detail: The two-dimensional layout and clusterings the publication map draws.

nodes.name: manifest.json
nodes.detail: Checksums and expected counts, checked before a bundle is served.

nodes.name: Keyword index
nodes.detail: Built from titles and abstracts when the library loads.

nodes.name: Query encoder
nodes.detail: Ships with the package and turns a query into a vector in about ten milliseconds, with no inference runtime.

nodes.name: Vector index
nodes.detail: The library's paper vectors, searched with an encoded query or a paper's own vector.

nodes.name: Collaboration graph
nodes.detail: Centrality, communities and joint papers over graph.json.

nodes.name: System prompt
nodes.detail: Names the cluster, the tools on offer and the proposal summary.

nodes.name: search_papers
nodes.detail: Keyword search over titles and abstracts; best for exact terms, acronyms and names.

nodes.name: semantic_search_papers
nodes.detail: Finds papers whose wording differs from the question's.

nodes.name: get_similar_papers
nodes.detail: The papers closest to one in the library.

nodes.name: locate_paper_by_doi
nodes.detail: Places a paper from outside the library among the cluster's closest work.

nodes.name: get_paper_by_doi
nodes.detail: Metadata and abstract for one DOI.

nodes.name: list_papers
nodes.detail: Every paper matching author, year and journal, newest first.

nodes.name: count_papers
nodes.detail: Counts papers mentioning terms, over abstracts and full texts.

nodes.name: search_fulltext
nodes.detail: Passages from the full texts that match a query. Chat only: passages around chosen queries would rebuild a paper.

nodes.name: get_paper_fulltext
nodes.detail: One paper's full text, or the passages that match a query. Chat only.

nodes.name: get_proposal_fulltext
nodes.detail: Searches the proposal's paragraphs. Chat only.

nodes.name: search_pis
nodes.detail: PIs whose profile matches a query.

nodes.name: list_pis
nodes.detail: Every PI with their number of papers in the library.

nodes.name: get_pi
nodes.detail: A PI's profile and their papers.

nodes.name: find_experts
nodes.detail: Who to ask about a topic, judged by their papers rather than their profile.

nodes.name: most_collaborative_papers
nodes.detail: The papers with the most of the cluster's PIs among the authors.

nodes.name: get_collaborators
nodes.detail: Everyone who has co-authored with a person, most shared papers first.

nodes.name: joint_papers
nodes.detail: The papers two people wrote together.

nodes.name: collaboration_centrality
nodes.detail: People ranked by betweenness, collaborators or shared papers.

nodes.name: collaboration_communities
nodes.detail: Groups of people who mostly publish with each other.

nodes.name: search_nomad
nodes.detail: Searches public NOMAD entries by elements, formula, author or text.

nodes.name: library_status
nodes.detail: Counts and capabilities, so the model can say what it can and cannot see.

nodes.group: Connected by the user · chat only
nodes.name: elab_*
nodes.detail: The tools of the user's own eLabFTW, through its MCP server. Listed only when read-only, unless the deployment allows writes.

nodes.group: Connected by the user · chat only
nodes.name: dt_*
nodes.detail: The tools of the user's own DataTagger, through its MCP server.

nodes.group: Connected by the user · chat only
nodes.name: nomad_*
nodes.detail: The user's own NOMAD, including unpublished uploads, through its MCP server. A deployment may hold a read-only key for chosen accounts.

nodes.name: Tool registry
nodes.detail: Every tool is declared once with the tier it needs. A caller is offered only what its tier allows, and calling anything else by name fails; nothing depends on a prompt.

nodes.name: Language model
nodes.detail: The model that answers. On OpenRouter it can be chosen automatically: the cheapest one that meets the account's guardrails.

nodes.name: Sign-in
nodes.detail: Password accounts, and institutional sign-in through DFN-AAI where configured. Everything but the landing page needs an account.

nodes.name: Connected sources
nodes.detail: Where a user connects their own eLabFTW, DataTagger or NOMAD. The token is kept per account, sealed, when the deployment has a key for it.

nodes.name: Chat
nodes.detail: The web assistant: a streaming tool-use loop over every tool the account may reach, plus its connected sources.

nodes.name: Publication map and collaboration graph
nodes.detail: The library drawn: papers by content, people by co-authorship. A DOI from outside can be placed on the map.

nodes.name: Outward MCP endpoint
nodes.detail: The same registry over streamable HTTP for Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor and others, with a token or an OAuth sign-in. Public tier only: no full text or proposal leaves through it. Rate-limited, and every call is audited.

nodes.name: History
nodes.detail: Conversations, and per answer the model, time taken and tool calls, which the usage figures above are counted from.

nodes.name: Feedback
nodes.detail: Bug reports and notes with the conversation they were sent from. Admins read them in the console or with cra feedback export.
